issues.legal_issue: Special leave may be revoked when it was obtained on the basis of a false and materially misleading factual assertion in the petition.
material_facts: The petitioner sought special leave after the High Court dismissed his second appeal in an eviction suit.
The special leave petition asserted that a rent note did not state that the landlord’s predecessor owned the shop.
The rent note expressly identified the predecessor as the owner, and that fact was decisive to the only issue said to arise in the case.
The petitioner offered no sufficient explanation for the false assertion.
issues.conclusion: The Court revoked the special leave, rejected the special leave petition, and vacated the stay.
issues.legal_principle: The Court’s discretionary jurisdiction under Article 136 is exercised sparingly and in exceptional cases. A person invoking it must come with clean hands; a material false or misleading statement that bears on the exercise of the Court’s discretion justifies refusing relief or revoking leave already granted. The Court followed and reiterated Hari Narain v. Badri Das, [1964] 2 SCR 203 at 209, and Rajabhai Abdul Rehman Munshi v. Vasudev Dhanjibhai Mody, [1964] 3 SCR 481 at 488 and 493.

predicates.special_leave_petition: A party asked the Supreme Court for special leave to appeal.
predicates.false_factual_assertion: The petitioner made a factual assertion that was contradicted by the relevant record.
predicates.assertion_material_to_grant: The contradicted assertion concerned a fact bearing decisively on whether leave should be granted.
predicates.special_leave_revoked: The Supreme Court withdrew the special leave it had granted.

issues.definition: When a party seeks special leave and makes a false factual assertion material to its grant, the output is that the granted leave is withdrawn.
